en.title: Minimum Box Moves After Minimizing the Warehouse Gap
en.description:
One move takes a box from a non-empty pile and puts it on another pile. First make the difference between the largest and smallest final piles as small as possible; among plans that achieve this minimum difference, find the minimum number of moves. Initial counts may repeat.

This site independently prepared the standard I/O and the solution; bounds supplemented where the source lacks them and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the specification.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n box counts. Original bounds: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤boxes[i]≤10^9; the total number of boxes stays the same, and no external difference parameter is given.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 2; 0; 6. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Let base=floor(sum/n), compute the total deficit D below base and the total excess E above base+1; the answer is max(D,E).
